node.title: DLI cyclic-band tensor and owner deletion
node.statement: Let n=4r and zeta have exact order n in an odd-characteristic field. For a uniform binary word, let E_1 and E_2 be the null events for the complete cyclic frequency bands {1+4l:0<=l<r} and {2+4l:0<=l<r}. Then P(E_1)=(4/16)^r, P(E_2)=(6/16)^r, and P(E_1 intersect E_2)=(2/16)^r, so their correlation excess is (4/3)^r. Every joint word is invariant under shift r and hence under the antipodal shift n/2, so primitive first-owner deletion makes the joint event empty. This does not control truncated low-frequency bands.
node.attack_surface: Check the s+ra index decomposition, outer Fourier invertibility, order-four local equations, exact 4/6/2 counts, tensor normalization, antipodal invariance, and complete-band versus truncated-prefix scope.
node.falsifier: A fixture where the complete-band null events do not localize to the stated four-point equations, the correlation ratio differs from (4/3)^r, or a joint word survives antipodal primitive deletion.
node.notes: This separates two facts: cyclic Fourier bands can correlate exponentially, but this canonical excess belongs entirely to the quotient-periodic owner already deleted by C2''. The unresolved object is the truncated primitive prefix.
